ambitions.title: Four of the charter’s faculties
ambitions.text: The founding charter names six faculties. {school} has one of them. The Provost has proposed saying publicly how many will exist by a named year, on the grounds that a college which will not name a number has not really decided to be one.
ambitions.kept: Four of the charter's six faculties stand, which is four more than the year it was promised in.
ambitions.missed: The year named for the faculties came and went with the charter still mostly a document.

ambitions.title: A thousand students on the lawn
ambitions.text: Convocation is held on the lawn because the hall will not hold everyone, which is a happier reason than it sounds. The Registrar has worked out what a thousand would look like and would like to know whether that is the plan or merely the trend.
ambitions.kept: A thousand of them on the lawn, and the hall never used for it again.
ambitions.missed: The thousand did not come. The lawn was booked anyway.

ambitions.title: A hundred million in the fund
ambitions.text: The Investment Committee has done the arithmetic on what the endowment would have to be for {school} to stop worrying about a bad year. The number is not a secret and the committee would like it to stop being a private one.
ambitions.kept: A hundred million, and a college that can survive a bad decade.
ambitions.missed: The fund fell short of the number the college had said out loud.

ambitions.title: The best teaching in the state
ambitions.text: A trustee has asked what {school} is actually for, in the tone of somebody who has an answer ready. The answer offered, and minuted, was teaching: not the largest college, not the richest, the one whose graduates say they were taught.
ambitions.kept: The teaching is what the college is known for, which is what it said it would be.
ambitions.missed: The teaching did not become what the college promised a trustee it would.

ambitions.title: Not one building on the register
ambitions.text: The Clerk keeps a register of buildings with work outstanding. It has never been empty. The proposal is to say, publicly and with a year attached, that it will be.
ambitions.kept: The register is empty for the first time since the founding.
ambitions.missed: The register was not empty on the day the college had named.

ambitions.title: Owing nothing to anybody
ambitions.text: The construction borrowing has been refinanced twice and explained to the board three times. The Bursar's paper this year is one page and ends with a date by which the college could owe nothing at all.
ambitions.kept: The college owes nothing to anybody, for the first time since it broke ground.
ambitions.missed: The date passed and the borrowing is still on the books.

ambitions.title: A full catalogue
ambitions.text: The prospectus is thin. The Registrar has costed a full one — every programme the founded schools could offer, taught properly — and has attached the costing to a proposed date, which is the part that makes it an announcement rather than a memo.
ambitions.kept: The catalogue is full, and every programme in it is taught.
ambitions.missed: The catalogue is still thin, and the date the college named is behind it.

ambitions.title: A campus worth the photograph
ambitions.text: A landscape architect has been round and was polite. Her report says that {school} has buildings and does not yet have a campus, and that the difference is about fifteen years of planting and one decision.
ambitions.kept: The campus is what the architect said it could be, fifteen years on.
ambitions.missed: The planting was not done, and the photographs are still of buildings.

ambitions.title: Alumni who answer the telephone
ambitions.text: The Development Office has the figures on what proportion of {school}'s graduates have ever given anything, and would rather present them privately. The proposal is a decade of doing the unglamorous thing — asking about them rather than for money.
ambitions.kept: The ledger is warm, and the annual fund shows it.
ambitions.missed: The ledger stayed cold. The Development Office has stopped circulating the figures.

ambitions.title: Turning people away
ambitions.text: {school} admits most of who applies, which is not a criticism and is not a plan either. The Dean of Admissions has proposed the other thing: fewer places, more applicants, and the years of patience in between.
ambitions.kept: The college turns people away now, and the classes show it.
ambitions.missed: The college is still admitting most of who asks.

ambitions.title: Out of the hole by the decade’s end
ambitions.text: The board has been discussing the college's position for four meetings. This meeting produced something different: a date, written down, by which {school} will be out of it, and an understanding that the date will be remembered.
ambitions.kept: The college came out of it by the date it had named, which almost nobody expected.
ambitions.missed: The date came. The college was still in the hole.

ambitions.title: Thirty scholars worth the name
ambitions.text: The roster is small enough that the Provost knows everyone's field and most of their arguments. The proposal is to stop being that college: thirty of them, properly paid, in a decade.
ambitions.kept: Thirty scholars, properly paid, and a Provost who no longer knows all the arguments.
ambitions.missed: The roster did not grow into what the college said it would.

lines.offered: The board has put something on the record: {title}.
lines.capReached: Three is as many promises as the college will make at once.
lines.note: A public commitment with a date on it. Declining costs nothing; keeping it is worth more than that.
